rca of the issue: Root cause: single missed rename in /app/backend/routes/team_routes.py. The PUT handler was already refactored (iter 5) to iterate SOCIAL_FIELDS via raw request.form(), so it picked up `facebook` automatically when SOCIAL_FIELDS was updated. The POST handler (create_team_member) still uses explicit per-field Form() params, so renaming required two edits that were missed: (1) the Form param declaration `orcid: Optional[str] = Form(default='')` on line 62, and (2) the ORM kwarg `orcid=_clean_social(orcid)` on line 91. The model already dropped the orcid column, so the kwarg call now raises TypeError at instance construction time, surfacing as a 500 to the client. Reproduction: `curl -X POST $BACKEND/api/admin/team -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -F 'name=X' -F 'role=Y'` → 500. Confirmed in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log: `TypeError: 'orcid' is an invalid keyword argument for TeamMember` at team_routes.py line 79. Mitigation (2 lines for main agent): replace both occurrences of `orcid` with `facebook` in team_routes.py (the Form param name on line 62 and the kwarg on line 91).
